title: A news agency and its subscribers

blocks.text: The page's analogy is a newspaper: the publisher (the **subject**) keeps a list of subscribers (the **observers**) and delivers each new edition to everyone on it. Subscribers join and leave at any time.
`Observer<T>` (given) has `void update(String event, T data)`. Write `NewsAgency`:

items: `addObserver(o)` registers `o`; `null` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. **An observer already registered** (by `equals`) **is not added again**.
`removeObserver(o)` unregisters `o`. **Removing an observer that is not registered does nothing** (no exception, also for `null`).

`publishArticle(article)` records the article, then calls `update("NEW_ARTICLE", article)` on every observer. **A blank article** (`null`, empty or only spaces) **is refused** with `IllegalArgumentException` before anyone is notified.
`getPublishedArticles()` returns the articles in publishing order; **the list a caller gets can never change the agency's record**.
`observerCount()` returns how many observers are registered.

cases.says: publishArticle() records the article and delivers it to every registered observer; a removed observer gets nothing more.
Adding an observer that is already registered (by equals) does not make it receive each article twice.
An article that is only spaces throws IllegalArgumentException, is not recorded and reaches nobody.
Changing the list returned by getPublishedArticles(), or trying to, never changes what the agency has recorded.
removeObserver() with an observer that was never added, or with null, does nothing and throws nothing.

concepts: A null observer or blank data is refused, while removing an unknown observer or notifying an empty list is a no-op.
A subject checks whether an observer is already registered before adding it, so no observer is notified twice.
A subject keeps a list of observers, lets them register and unregister at runtime, and calls each one's update() when its state changes.
Published data exposed to clients is returned as an unmodifiable view or a copy, never the subject's own list.
